rationale:
Issue #253 (labeled 'bug') reports that the documented form `{% if (one or two) and three %}` fails with a dangling-token error because token components are split on whitespace only, so parentheses must be space-surrounded. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in Sources/Tokenizer.swift that, inside appendWord, peels a leading '(' or trailing ')' off a word into its own component and recurses on the remainder — exactly the whitespace-only splitting defect described. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test edit from the same fixing commit: IfNodeSpec's existing 'can parse an if with complex expression' case changes its block value to `if value == "test" and (not name or not (name and surname))`, which contains `(not` and `surname))` and therefore exercises only the patched path; it uses pre-existing Token/if-parsing entry points and no API introduced by the fix. Patch scope is production-behavior only: 6 added lines, no formatting, refactor, docs, or config change (the CHANGELOG and later cleanup commits ab4b136/e70023d/59ca064/e4090c7 of PR #254 are excluded). The build-compatibility patch touches only a test file, qualifying `Expression` as `Stencil.Expression` to avoid a Swift 6 Foundation name collision, and is applied symmetrically to buggy and fixed revisions without altering assertions. Traceability is fix_commit_to_merged_pr_to_issue via PR #254 ('Resolves #253'). Machine-generated strict gates pass both pre- and post-minimization: build on both revisions, buggy differential on Tests/StencilTests/IfNodeSpec.swift::testIfNode, deterministic across 3 repetitions (32 matrix runs), fixed isolated/suite/reversed clean, and fixed full suite all green with buggy full-suite failures limited to the reproduced trigger. No active same-project root causes are registered, and stencilproject/stencil#253 is in allowed_root_cause_ids.

Issue #253 (labeled 'bug') reports that documented syntax `{% if (one or two) and three %}` throws a dangling-token error because token components are split on whitespace only, so parentheses must be space-surrounded. The single retained production hunk in Sources/Tokenizer.swift addresses exactly that: a word with a leading '(' or trailing ')' (and not equal to the bare bracket) is decomposed into a separate bracket component plus a recursive appendWord on the remainder. Traceability is fix_commit_to_merged_pr_to_issue via merged PR #254 ('Resolves #253'), whose title matches the commit subject. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test hunk from the same fixing commit: IfNodeSpec's 'can parse an if with complex expression' input becomes `if value == "test" and (not name or not (name and surname))`, containing `(not` and `surname))` — the exact non-space-delimited parenthesis forms in the issue. It uses only pre-existing Token/.block and if-parsing entry points and introduces no API added by the fix. Strict evidence shows both revisions build, the declared selector Tests/StencilTests/IfNodeSpec.swift::testIfNode fails alone on the buggy revision and is the only buggy full-suite failure, fixed isolated/suite/reversed runs are clean, determinism holds over 3 repetitions (32 matrix runs), and the same gate set passes post-minimization (1 of 1 hunk retained, 0 removed). The only auxiliary change is a test-file-scoped build-compatibility edit qualifying `Expression` as `Stencil.Expression` in ExpressionSpec.swift to avoid a Swift 6 Foundation name collision, applied symmetrically to both revisions with no assertion or production-logic effect; the production patch itself contains no refactor, formatting, feature, docs, or config change. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and the proposed root cause matches the sole allowed verified issue key.
